title: Common-source gain, input and output impedance

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
With the small-signal model in hand, the common-source stage reduces to a one-line result. The input drives the gate, which is insulated, so the input resistance is infinite at low frequency and any source resistance costs nothing. The controlled source \(g_mv_{in}\) pulls current out of the drain node, which sees \(r_o\) in parallel with the load resistor. The output voltage is that current times the parallel resistance, with a minus sign: the stage inverts. Zero the input and only \(r_o\) and \(R_D\) remain, so they also give the output resistance.

Two rewrites are worth knowing. First, any external load just joins the parallel combination; that is the two-port divider in disguise. Second, using \(g_m = 2I_D/V_{ov}\), the resistor-loaded gain is \(2V_{RD}/V_{ov}\), the DC drop across \(R_D\) over half the overdrive. High gain with a resistor therefore needs a large DC drop, which runs out of supply quickly. The ceiling, reached as the load resistance goes to infinity, is the intrinsic gain \(g_mr_o\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ A_v = -g_m(r_o\parallel R_D\parallel R_L), \qquad R_{in} = \infty, \qquad R_{out} = r_o\parallel R_D \]
\[ |A_v| \approx g_mR_D = \frac{2V_{RD}}{V_{ov}}, \qquad |A_v|_{\max} = g_mr_o \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A CS stage biased at \(I_D = 0.3\ \mathrm{mA}\) with \(V_{ov} = 0.3\ \mathrm{V}\) has \(g_m = 2\ \mathrm{mS}\). With \(R_D = 6\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) and \(r_o = 30\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\), the drain sees 5 kΩ, so \(A_v = -10\) and \(R_{out} = 5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). The 1.8 V drop across \(R_D\) predicts \(2(1.8)/0.3 = 12\) before \(r_o\) is included.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Forgetting \(r_o\) or an attached load in the parallel combination.
- Dividing by the source resistance; at low frequency the gate takes no current.
- Raising \(R_D\) for gain without checking that the device stays saturated.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Running out of headroom motivates current-source loads. Cascading CS stages multiplies gains, and the capacitances at the gate and drain set the stage's bandwidth.
